extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys) and USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO disciplinary sanction and compliance terms
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order setting forth jurisdiction, stipulated facts, legal conclusions, sanctions (public reprimand and probation), and detailed compliance/reporting obligations for a registered patent practitioner found to have engaged in disreputable conduct. Includes the process and consequences for noncompliance (Order to Show Cause and possible suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26; Respondent is a registered agent subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the legal basis for disciplining registered practitioners and confirms applicability of the USPTO disciplinary rules to the respondent; citation of the specific statutory and regulatory provisions used to assert jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline — disreputable conduct and adverse reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent admits conduct that violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) (engaging in disreputable conduct) and 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) (engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the regulatory provisions constituting the misconduct; factual basis here is failure to timely file/pay federal and state income taxes for multiple years leading to tax delinquencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions imposed — public reprimand and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is publicly reprimanded and placed on probation for eighty-eight months; Respondent is permitted to practice patent law before the USPTO during probation unless subsequently suspended or excluded by order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Order sets specific sanction types and duration; permits continued practice subject to probationary conditions and potential subsequent suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger and process for suspension during probation (Order to Show Cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's last address of record, and grant Respondent fifteen days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after considering Respondent's response (if any), the OED Director still believes noncompliance occurred, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and supporting evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to twenty-four months. This entry captures the procedural steps (issue, service, 15-day response period, transmission to USPTO Director, and suspension request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the notice of reprimand and probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires public posting of disciplinary decisions and a Gazette notice summarizing the reprimand, probation, and the conduct leading to discipline; also requires compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 (notification requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation notification exception when not representing clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on Respondent's representation that he is currently not representing other persons before the Office in patent matters, the probation notification requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4) do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that certain notification obligations depend on whether the practitioner represents clients at the time of discipline; if representing clients, § 11.20(a)(4) would apply and impose additional notification duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial remediation obligations (payment agreements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with the Payment Agreement with the IRS (four semi-annual payments of $2,585.14) and the Payment Agreement with Maryland (monthly payments of $466.13 for eighty-eight months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies concrete payment terms the practitioner must meet as conditions of the settlement; failure to make timely payments constitutes a violation of the Agreement and Final Order and triggers the Order to Show Cause process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic and event-driven reporting obligations during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commencing the first business day of the month after the Final Order is signed, and every three months thereafter until probation ends, Respondent shall submit to the OED Director an affidavit attesting to compliance with the IRS and Maryland Payment Agreements and corroborating proof (copies of correspondence and payment remittances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting is quarterly; requires affidavits plus documentary proof of payments and correspondence. This creates an ongoing monitoring obligation tied to the probation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of correspondence with tax authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: During probation, Respondent must submit to the OED Director copies of all correspondence to and from Respondent and the IRS about the Payment Agreement with the IRS within ten business days of the date of such correspondence; likewise for correspondence with the State of Maryland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event-driven reporting: any correspondence (including modifications, notices of default, notices of breach) must be produced to OED within 10 business days, enabling rapid OED awareness of problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual federal tax transcript disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall submit to the OED Director by June 1, 2012, and by the first day of June each year thereafter during probation, a copy of his official federal tax return transcript and his official federal tax account transcript (see IRS Form 4506-T) for the preceding tax year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual verification of federal tax compliance via official IRS transcripts; example timeline provided (2011 transcripts by June 1, 2012; 2012 transcripts by June 1, 2013, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences regarding USPTO customer numbers and PKI upon suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended, the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates; Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated, and may not obtain a customer number or PKI certificate unless reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and technical measures to prevent access/use of USPTO electronic resources during suspension; also states that review of a suspension will not stay the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED and Office may seek further discipline and use record as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57 for misconduct that caused suspension; the Office may consider the record of this proceeding (including the Final Order) when addressing future complaints as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits the disciplinary record to be used in future proceedings and does not preclude additional sanctions for related misconduct; signals enduring consequences of the disciplinary finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to comply with payment or reporting obligations triggers enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent fails for any reason to make timely payments to the IRS or the Comptroller of Maryland, or otherwise fails to comply with reporting obligations, he shall be in violation of the Agreement and Final Order, and the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause pursuant to the suspension process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links specific covenant breaches (financial or reporting) to the procedural enforcement mechanism (Order to Show Cause → potential suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party responsible for its own expenses; no award of costs between parties as part of this settlement.
